cells.B2: Timesheet reporting should be available by both month and week.
cells.B3: The Timesheet per Week report should be generated using a pivot-based structure, enabling better tracking of workload distribution, identification of peaks or delays, and early detection of schedule risks.
cells.B4: Introduce a Remaining Hours metric for improved project visibility, allowing Project Managers to quickly assess delivery risk without manually interpreting purchased versus consumed hours.
cells.B5: Add Task Estimation Accuracy per Employee (Spent Hours / Planned Hours) to support continuous improvement by identifying estimation gaps and resource planning inefficiencies.
cells.B6: Add resource distribution per project, segmented by role (BA, PM, Technical), to support capacity planning, role balance analysis, and staffing decisions across projects.
cells.B7: Add reporting for tasks stuck for more than a defined number of days, by stage, to enable proactive intervention before delays impact milestones or delivery commitments.
cells.B8: Add reporting for AR versus CR count and associated time consumption to provide insight into scope evolution, change impact, and contractual risk, helping distinguish planned work from reactive or out-of-scope effort.
cells.B9: Add Reopened Task Count, including employee-level analysis where feasible, to highlight rework patterns and potential quality or requirement gaps.
cells.B10: Add Phase Distribution reporting to provide clarity on where effort is being consumed across delivery phases, enabling better forecasting and prioritization.
cells.B11: Add Maximum Waiting Stage to expose workflow inefficiencies and approval or dependency bottlenecks.
cells.B12: Add Bucket Distribution reporting to provide clarity on where effort is being consumed across delivery phases, enabling better forecasting and prioritization.
cells.B13: Add Average Time in Stage to expose workflow inefficiencies and approval or dependency bottlenecks.
cells.B14: Weekly charts displayed as W32, W33, etc. are not intuitive for interpretation.
cells.B15: Viewing multiple projects simultaneously causes data to be mixed, reducing clarity and traceability.
cells.B16: Timesheet per week reports do not clearly indicate the corresponding month.
cells.B17: The dashboard structure and milestone framework are not sufficiently flexible or standardized, limiting effective reporting for projects both with and without milestones.
cells.B18: The dashboard presents only aggregated KPIs without interactive drill-down or URL redirection to underlying task records, limiting auditability and making data validation time-consuming.
cells.B19: The calculation logic for the “Timesheet on Completed” metric is unclear.
cells.B20: Tasks that are not milestone-driven (e.g., External Communication) are not adequately represented.
cells.B21: Remaining Hours are not displayed; only Purchased versus Consumed hours are shown.
cells.B22: Maintenance tasks may not be consistently or accurately reflected in reporting.
cells.B23: KPI color logic is not consistently aligned with business meaning; for example, an Over Budget value of zero should be displayed in green rather than red to accurately reflect a healthy project state.
cells.B24: For single-project views, filters such as Project Manager and Team Leader add limited value.
cells.B25: Applied filters are cleared upon page refresh, resulting in repetitive user effort.
